Detestable
dē-tĕs´ta-bl
adj. (utterly abhorrent; rendering Hebrew shiqquts)
From Latin detestari, to curse while calling the gods to witness. Detestable is the strongest available word for what God abhors.

Biblical Definition

Detestable means utterly abhorrent, and in the prophets it is a technical word for idols. Jeremiah charges Israel: “they set their abominations in the house, which is called by my name, to defile it” (Jer 32:34), and Ezekiel repeatedly names “all the detestable things thereof and all the abominations thereof” (Eze 5:11; 7:20; 11:18,21). The word marks the objects that made the temple unfit for the God whose name it bore.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines detestable as extremely hateful; abominable; very odious; deserving abhorrence.

expand to see more

DETESTABLE, a. Extremely hateful; abominable; very odious; deserving abhorrence.

DETEST, v.t. To abhor; to abominate; to hate extremely; as, to detest crimes or meanness.

Key Scripture

Eze 5:11 — "Wherefore, as I live, saith the Lord GOD; Surely, because thou hast defiled my sanctuary with all thy detestable things, and with all thine abominations, therefore will I also diminish thee; neither shall mine eye spare, neither will I have any pity."

Eze 11:18 — "And they shall come thither, and they shall take away all the detestable things thereof and all the abominations thereof from thence."

Eze 7:20 — "As for the beauty of his ornament, he set it in majesty: but they made the images of their abominations and of their detestable things therein: therefore have I set it far from them."

Jer 32:34 — "But they set their abominations in the house, which is called by my name, to defile it."

Modern Corruption

Idolatry is imagined as worshipping statues elsewhere, and Ezekiel's detestable things were installed inside the temple by people who still used God's name.

expand to see more

Ezekiel 5:11 states the offence and the consequence in one sentence: because thou hast defiled my sanctuary with all thy detestable things, and with all thine abominations, therefore will I also diminish thee. The detestable things were not in a rival temple; they were in His. Ezekiel 8 takes the prophet on a tour of them — an image of jealousy at the gate, creeping things portrayed on the walls, women weeping for Tammuz, and twenty-five men with their backs to the temple worshipping the sun.

Ezekiel 11:18 contains the promise that answers it, and the order matters: and they shall come thither, and they shall take away all the detestable things thereof and all the abominations thereof from thence. And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. The removal and the new heart belong to the same act of God, which is why reform that only removes objects has never yet held.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew shiqquts (H8251), a detestable thing, idol; toebah (H8441), abomination; gillulim (H1544), dung-idols.

expand to see more

Hebrew shiqquts (H8251) — detestable thing, idol; Ezekiel 5:11, 7:20, 11:18, 21, Jeremiah 16:18.

Hebrew toebah (H8441) — abomination; the constant companion word.

Hebrew gillulim (H1544) — idols; Ezekiel's contemptuous term throughout.

Usage

"“Thou hast defiled my sanctuary with all thy detestable things” — installed in His own house."

"“They shall take away all the detestable things… and I will give them one heart” — removal and renewal together."

"“They set their abominations in the house, which is called by my name” — the name still in use."
